target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures focus on Data Center revenue performance for the fiscal year summary. 2023_D021 cites $15.01B (implied by context of D030) and 41% growth driven by hyperscalers and CSP partners. 2024_D018 cites $47.5B (in D024) and 217% growth driven by enterprise/verticals. While D018 is the summary row, it covers the same specific financial topic as D021 (Fiscal Year Summary Data Center). D024 is the detailed Market Platform Highlight for Data Center, which corresponds to D030.

2024_D025 focuses on Data Center customer concentration (cloud providers >50% revenue) and automotive data center trends. 2023_D021 explicitly mentions 'purchases made by several CSP partners to support multi-year cloud service agreements' as a driver for Data Center revenue. This is the most direct prior-year link to the 'large cloud providers' and 'CSP' focus in 2024_D025. 2023_D030 also mentions hyperscaler/cloud usage, but D021 is more specific to the partner/customer relationship structure.

previous_disclosures.summary: Data Center revenue increased 41% year-over-year, driven by hyperscale customers, CSP partners supporting cloud service agreements, and R&D activities.

current_disclosures.summary: Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 increased 217%, driven by strong demand in enterprise software, consumer internet, and verticals such as automotive, financial services, and healthcare; compute revenue rose 244% and networking revenue rose 133%.

In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024, large cloud providers represented more than half of Data Center revenue. Additionally, the company expects NVIDIA's automotive data center processing demand to grow significantly as AV algorithms shift to video transformers.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD agreed to acquire ZT Group Int'l, Inc. (ZT Systems) in August 2024 to extend data center infrastructure capabilities and accelerate time to market for AI solutions, with expected closure in the first half of fiscal 2025 subject to regulatory approvals and intent to seek a strategic partner for ZT's manufacturing business.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose strategic initiatives specifically aimed at extending and accelerating their data center infrastructure capabilities for AI workloads. NVDA highlights a market driver where large cloud providers constituted more than half of Data Center revenue in Q4 FY2024, supporting its focus on data center processing demand. AMD mirrors this infrastructure focus through its acquisition of ZT Systems, explicitly stating the intent to 'extend our data center infrastructure capabilities' and 'accelerate time to market for our leadership AI training and inferencing solutions' for hyperscale computing companies.

sentences.text: In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024, large cloud providers represented more than half of our Data Center revenue, supporting both internal workloads and external customers.

We also focused on extending our data center infrastructure capabilities by entering into an agreement in August 2024 to acquire ZT Group Int'l, Inc. (ZT Systems), a provider of AI and general purpose compute infrastructure for hyperscale computing companies.
We believe that with the acquisition of ZT Systems, we can accelerate time to market for our leadership AI training and inferencing solutions.
